newsitem.title: JORDAN: Mideast uncertainty continues to hit Jordan stocks.
newsitem.headline: Mideast uncertainty continues to hit Jordan stocks.

text.p: Jordanian stocks, harmed by Middle East tension, dropped slightly at the close of weekly trade on Wednesday but some brokers reported renewed foreign investor interest in the region's most politically-sensitive bourse.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index dropped 0.01 percent to 147.59 points from 147.60 points on Tuesday.
"There is a wait-and-see mood because of the general political climate in the area," said broker Samir Jaradat.
"But we do not expect to see any further drops in the near future," he told Reuters.
In Washington, leaders of the United States, Israel, Jordan and the Palestinians delayed planned Middle East summit talks.
"Everyone's eyes are on the summit," said another broker.
"Foreign clients are still looking with keen eye on the Jordanian market but are very cautious because they would like to see stability before they move."

Brokers reported renewed "non-Jordanian" interest in market leader Arab Bank, the bourses most expensive share. But its price remained unchanged for the fourth consecutive day at 242 dinars after it propelled the index upwards in the first half of September.
The Middle East Investment Bank also remained unchanged at 1.06 dinars. .
A total of 238,670 shares changed hands for 497,902 dinars ($710,270) in select blue chips buying.
After gradual gains earlier this month that sent the market back above 150 points last week for the first time in four months, shares began to hit down-limits on political violence last Tuesday.
Brokers fear the market may be running out of steam as institutional investors continue to wait in the sidelines and stocks run into profit-taking after the bourse's recent results-driven rally.
Industrials led the market on Wednesday, followed by banks and services.
